novel_features.name: New-since diff
novel_features.description: See only the Amazon reqs that appeared since you last synced a saved search — no more re-scanning the whole list every morning.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a stored id_icims cursor in the local SQLite store; the stateless search API has no notion of 'new since my last look'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a user tracks a role over time and wants the delta, not the full list.

novel_features.name: Saved searches
novel_features.description: Persist a named query plus its filters and diff cursor so a search and its new-since state survive between runs.
novel_features.rationale: Persists {name, query, filters, cursor} rows the stateless API cannot hold.
novel_features.example: amazon-jobs-pp-cli save sde-seattle "software engineer" --city Seattle --country USA
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to set up a repeatable watch that `new` and `sync` then operate on by name.

novel_features.name: Facet aggregation
novel_features.description: Count synced reqs grouped by city, state, team, or category — the aggregation Amazon's own empty facets[] never returns.
novel_features.rationale: GROUP BY over the local store; the server does zero aggregation and broad live counts are capped at 10000.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'which cities/teams have the most open reqs' without paging every result.

novel_features.name: Qualification-demand scan
novel_features.description: Rank teams and cities by how many synced reqs demand a given skill keyword in their basic/preferred qualifications.
novel_features.rationale: Keyword scan over qualification text grouped by team/city in local SQLite — cross-field demand no single API call returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for labor-market questions like 'who is hiring for X skill' rather than retrieving individual reqs.

novel_features.name: Pipeline facet filters
novel_features.description: Filter live results by intern, manager, university, and schedule type — fields the .json endpoint silently ignores as server params.
novel_features.rationale: NULL-safe client-side predicates over paged results (scan-and-filter, --max-scan-pages bound); those fields are frequently null and non-filterable server-side.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use these flags when a user wants senior-IC, non-intern, or schedule-specific roles that Amazon can't filter server-side.

narrative.headline: Every Amazon.jobs feature, plus a local job store, new-since diffing, and aggregation Amazon's own site can't do — no login required.
narrative.value_prop: amazon-jobs turns Amazon's careers site from a page you refresh into a queryable, watchable dataset. It uses the same unauthenticated JSON the site does, so there is no API key and no scraping fragility. Beyond search and filters, it keeps a local SQLite mirror that powers `new` (reqs unseen since your last check), `stats` (counts by city/team/category the empty server facets can't give), and `skills` (which teams demand a given qualification).

quickstart.comment: Confirm the API is reachable (no auth needed).
Search live listings by keyword and country.
Agent-native output, narrowed to the fields that matter (skips the huge description).

quickstart.command: amazon-jobs-pp-cli save sde-seattle "software engineer" --city Seattle --country USA
quickstart.comment: Persist a named search to track over time.
Mirror listings into the local store.
Aggregate the synced store by city — counts Amazon's site never shows.

troubleshoots.symptom: A search with filters returns zero results but the same query without filters returns thousands.
troubleshoots.fix: Always pass --limit >= 1; the API returns 0 hits when result_limit is 0 combined with a location filter.

troubleshoots.symptom: `new` or `stats` says the local mirror is empty.
troubleshoots.fix: Run `amazon-jobs-pp-cli sync engineer` (or `sync` a saved search) first to populate the store.

troubleshoots.symptom:
Job descriptions are full of
and HTML entities.
troubleshoots.fix: Add --plain to `find`/`get` to strip HTML into readable text.

troubleshoots.symptom: Broad searches always report about 10000 hits.
troubleshoots.fix: That is Amazon's server-side cap for broad queries; narrow with keyword/location filters, or sync and use `stats` for exact local counts.

narrative.when_to_use: Use amazon-jobs when a task involves finding, filtering, tracking, or analyzing open roles at Amazon or AWS: keyword and location search, watching for newly-posted reqs over time, or aggregating the open-req landscape by city, team, or demanded skill. It is ideal for agents doing recurring labor-market research because output is deterministic JSON and the local store answers questions a single API call cannot.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for job boards other than Amazon.jobs — it only queries Amazon's careers API.
Do not use it to submit an application; it is read-only and has no apply/authenticated workflow.
Do not use it for general AWS service management — it is unrelated to the AWS SDK or AWS APIs.

recipes.title: Track new SDE roles in Seattle each morning
recipes.command: amazon-jobs-pp-cli save sde-seattle "software engineer" --city Seattle --country USA && amazon-jobs-pp-cli new sde-seattle --agent
recipes.explanation: Persist a named search once, then run `new` to see only reqs that appeared since your last sync.

recipes.title: Agent-native search narrowed to key fields
recipes.explanation: Amazon reqs carry huge description/qualification text; --select trims the payload to the fields an agent needs.

recipes.title: Where is AWS hiring most right now?
recipes.command: amazon-jobs-pp-cli sync aws --max-pages 10 && amazon-jobs-pp-cli stats --by city
recipes.explanation: Mirror AWS reqs locally, then aggregate by city — counts the empty server facets never return.

recipes.title: Which teams demand a specific skill
recipes.command: amazon-jobs-pp-cli sync engineer --max-pages 10 && amazon-jobs-pp-cli skills Rust --agent
recipes.explanation: Scan synced qualification text for a keyword and rank teams/cities by demand.

recipes.explanation: Client-side NULL-safe filters for fields Amazon can't filter server-side.
